_README: Phase 3 deliverable (plan §6.2, agent literature-scout), produced interactively 2026-09-19. Every entry was resolved through the NCBI E-utilities from a DOI or a PubMed query; nothing is recalled from memory. `quote` is copied verbatim out of the paper's own PMC full text where the article is open access, and out of its PubMed abstract otherwise -- `quote_source` says which, so an abstract is never passed off as a full-text passage. A paper that could not be opened is not here.
gap_statement: Cross-platform transcriptomic harmonization has been benchmarked repeatedly, and each benchmark states a criterion: correlation with a reference, classifier accuracy, cluster separation, or a composite of single-cell integration metrics. No published study asks whether those criteria elect the same approaches. Article 2 measures that on 2,234 harmonization approaches and reports the overlap between the sets each metric class elects.

references.title: Transcriptomic Harmonization as the Way for Suppressing Cross-Platform Bias and Batch Effect
references.supports_claim: Harmonization quality is judged by a heterogeneous set of criteria — correlation, PCA inspection, clustering metrics — with no single agreed standard; this review is the field's own statement of that, and Article 2 measures what follows from it.
references.quote: The following quantitative metrics and methods may be applied to estimate the effect of harmonization: (1) First, different statistical criteria may be used to estimate the following endpoints: (a) Correlation analysis for the gene expression profiles before and after harmonization [29,30,31,33,34];
references.quote_section: 3. Evaluation of the Quality of Harmonization

references.title: Transcriptomic Harmonization as the Way for Suppressing Cross-Platform Bias and Batch Effect
references.supports_claim: Early cross-platform harmonization benchmarks judged success by eye, which is the practice Article 2's recipe replaces with a stated metric per class.
references.quote: Thus, early approaches used visual inspection of the principal component analysis (PCA) plots and/or cluster dendrograms to assess the cross-platform harmonization benchmarks [30,31,32,33,34].
references.quote_section: 3. Evaluation of the Quality of Harmonization

references.title: Shambhala: a platform-agnostic data harmonizer for gene expression data
references.supports_claim: Shambhala is the platform-agnostic harmonizer whose canonical variant is method 20_shambhala in this benchmark; cited for the method, not for a finding.
references.quote: In this study, we developed a new method termed Shambhala suitable for the universal, platform-agnostic harmonization.

references.title: Shambhala-2: A Protocol for Uniformly Shaped Harmonization of Gene Expression Profiles of Various Formats
references.supports_claim: Shambhala-2 is the protocol form of the same harmonizer, and the reference for the uniformly shaped output the benchmark's Shambhala runs produce.
references.quote: Uniformly shaped harmonization of gene expression profiles is central for the simultaneous comparison of multiple gene expression datasets.
references.quote_source: PubMed abstract — full text is not open access

references.title: Tackling the widespread and critical impact of batch effects in high-throughput data
references.supports_claim: Batch effects are widespread and become a major problem when correlated with the outcome of interest — the general framing of the Introduction.
references.quote: This becomes a major problem when batch effects are correlated with an outcome of interest and lead to incorrect conclusions.

references.title: Methods that remove batch effects while retaining group differences may lead to exaggerated confidence in downstream analyses
references.supports_claim: When study groups are not evenly distributed across batches, batch adjustment biases group differences and inflates confidence downstream. This is the theoretical backing for trap 3 and for reporting A_confirmed_bad with its confound stated.
references.quote: Thirdly, instead of ComBat, analyses of the real data with limma blocking by batch.

references.title: Batch effect removal methods for microarray gene expression data integration: a survey
references.supports_claim: A survey of batch-effect removal methods for expression data integration, cited once for the size of the method space Article 1 sampled.
references.quote: It has been acknowledged that the main source of variation between different MAGE datasets is due to the so-called 'batch effects'.
references.quote_source: PubMed abstract — full text is not open access

references.title: Adjusting batch effects in microarray expression data using empirical Bayes methods
references.supports_claim: ComBat, the empirical-Bayes location-scale adjustment behind the ComBat family that Article 2's prediction ranking elects.
references.quote: We propose parametric and non-parametric empirical Bayes frameworks for adjusting data for batch effects that is robust to outliers in small sample sizes and performs comparable to existing methods for large samples.
references.quote_source: PubMed abstract — full text is not open access

references.title: ComBat-seq: batch effect adjustment for RNA-seq count data
references.supports_claim: ComBat-seq, the count-based variant; one of the two implementations that tie exactly on the Group M margin.
references.quote: ComBat-seq is able to preserve the integer nature of count data, making the analysis pipeline more compatible for RNA-seq studies.

references.title: Feature specific quantile normalization enables cross-platform classification of molecular subtypes using gene expression data
references.supports_claim: Feature-specific quantile normalization, the method Article 1 selected for the SOM and one of the clustermap best approaches.
references.quote: We achieve up to 98% accuracy for BRCA data and 97% accuracy for CRC data in assigning molecular subtypes to RNA-seq data normalized using FSQN and a support vector machine trained exclusively on DNA microarray data.

references.title: Cross-platform normalization of microarray and RNA-seq data for machine learning applications
references.supports_claim: Cross-platform normalization of microarray and RNA-seq data judged by downstream classifier accuracy — a benchmark that used one criterion, which is the practice Article 2 questions.
references.quote: Nonparanormal transformation resulted in the best classification of Basal and LumA.

references.title: Bias in error estimation when using cross-validation for model selection
references.supports_claim: Cross-validation used for model selection gives an optimistically biased error estimate unless the selection is inside the loop — the reason Article 2 reports the worst multiclass fold beside the mean.
references.quote: In this article, we investigate the effect on the bias when using this nested CV approach.

references.title: Benchmarking atlas-level data integration in single-cell genomics
references.supports_claim: The scIB benchmark defines the composite of batch-correction and bio-conservation metrics that Article 1's local metrics descend from, and states that metrics disagree about which integration method wins.
references.quote: The x axis shows the overall batch correction score and the y axis shows the overall bio-conservation score.
references.quote_section: scATAC-seq integration performance depends on feature space

references.title: A test metric for assessing single-cell RNA-seq batch correction
references.supports_claim: kBET is a test for whether batches are locally well mixed; it was designed for single-cell data, which is the point Article 2 makes about borrowing it.
references.quote: Here we present a user-friendly, robust and sensitive k-nearest-neighbor batch-effect test (kBET; https://github.com/theislab/kBET ) for quantification of batch effects.
references.quote_source: PubMed abstract — full text is not open access

references.title: Fast, sensitive and accurate integration of single-cell data with Harmony
references.supports_claim: Harmony introduced the LISI family used as a local mixing metric in this benchmark.
references.quote: Accurate integration should maintain a cLISI of 1, reflecting a separation of unique cell types throughout the embedding.
references.quote_section: Quantifying Performance in Cell Line Data

references.title: A benchmark of batch-effect correction methods for single-cell RNA sequencing data
references.supports_claim: A single-cell batch-correction benchmark whose ranking depends on which metric is used — the same phenomenon Article 2 quantifies for bulk cross-platform data.
references.quote: The computed values of benchmarking metrics can be found in Additional file 5: Table S4, while the statistical tests for significance are in Additional file 6: Table S5.
references.quote_section: Comprehensive benchmarking of 14 methods on ten datasets using five evaluation metrics

references.title: Batch effects in single-cell RNA-sequencing data are corrected by matching mutual nearest neighbors
references.supports_claim: Mutual nearest neighbours, the MNN method Article 1's clustermap elected.
references.quote: We present a strategy for batch correction that is based on the detection of mutual nearest neighbours (MNN) in the high-dimensional expression space.

references.title: Distinct types of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma identified by gene expression profiling
references.supports_claim: Expression profiling splits DLBCL into germinal-centre and activated B-cell types — the biology the marker panel and the LOBO class labels encode.
references.quote: One type expressed genes characteristic of germinal centre B cells ('germinal centre B-like DLBCL'); the second type expressed genes normally induced during in vitro activation of peripheral blood B cells ('activated B-like DLBCL').
references.quote_source: PubMed abstract — full text is not open access

references.title: The use of molecular profiling to predict survival after chemotherapy for diffuse large-B-cell lymphoma
references.journal: The New England journal of medicine
references.supports_claim: Molecular profiling predicts survival after chemotherapy in DLBCL, the clinical motivation for signatures that must transfer across cohorts.
references.quote: We used the gene-expression profiles of these lymphomas to develop a molecular predictor of survival.
references.quote_source: PubMed abstract — full text is not open access

references.title: Determining cell-of-origin subtypes of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma using gene expression in formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue
references.supports_claim: Lymph2Cx assigns DLBCL cell-of-origin from FFPE material, the platform-transfer problem in its clinical form.
references.quote: In the validation cohort, the assay was accurate, with only 1 case with definitive COO being incorrectly assigned, and robust, with >95% concordance of COO assignment between 2 independent laboratories.

references.title: Prediction of survival in follicular lymphoma based on molecular features of tumor-infiltrating immune cells
references.journal: The New England journal of medicine
references.supports_claim: Survival in follicular lymphoma is predicted by immune-cell signatures of the microenvironment, which is why the marker panel carries TME signatures.
references.quote: The length of survival among patients with follicular lymphoma correlates with the molecular features of nonmalignant immune cells present in the tumor at diagnosis.
references.quote_source: PubMed abstract — full text is not open access

references.title: A gene-expression profiling score for prediction of outcome in patients with follicular lymphoma: a retrospective training and validation analysis in three international cohorts
references.supports_claim: A 23-gene expression score predicts outcome in follicular lymphoma — a signature whose portability across platforms is exactly what harmonization decides.
references.quote: It is uncertain whether the same limitation would be observed with gene-expression profiling of the tumors.

references.title: Molecular subtypes of diffuse large B cell lymphoma are associated with distinct pathogenic mechanisms and outcomes
references.supports_claim: Genetic subtypes of DLBCL with distinct outcomes, cited for disease heterogeneity.
references.quote: Patients with C2 DLBCLs had a distinct trajectory and a steady rate of progression over time (Fig. 6k,l and Supplementary Fig. 16a).

references.title: Genetics and Pathogenesis of Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
references.journal: The New England journal of medicine
references.supports_claim: Genetics and pathogenesis of DLBCL, the companion genetic classification.
references.quote: Overall, we classified 44.8% of our samples into these genetically “pure” subtypes of DLBCL and recognize that non-subtyped cases may share genetic features as well as etiologic factors with the genetic subtypes (Fig. 2B).

references.title: Merging two gene-expression studies via cross-platform normalization
references.supports_claim: XPN, the cross-platform normalization that merges two expression studies; method 26_xpn in this benchmark.
references.quote: This article considers the problem of how to merge datasets arising from different gene-expression studies of a common organism and phenotype.
references.quote_source: PubMed abstract — full text is not open access

references.title: Empirical comparison of cross-platform normalization methods for gene expression data
references.supports_claim: An empirical comparison of cross-platform normalization methods — a benchmark that ranked methods on one criterion, which is the practice Article 2 tests.
references.quote: By comparing these curves we obtain statistics for over and under-detection of differentially expressed genes after cross-platform normalization as follows.

references.title: Capturing heterogeneity in gene expression studies by surrogate variable analysis
references.supports_claim: Surrogate variable analysis, the basis of method 04_sva, which Article 1's clustermap elected and Article 2 carries as a named group.
references.quote: This justifies the use of the singular value decomposition to identify orthogonal signatures of expression heterogeneity for surrogate variable estimates.

references.title: Normalization of RNA-seq data using factor analysis of control genes or samples
references.supports_claim: RUV, factor analysis of control genes; method 09_ruv in the benchmark and the reference for the housekeeping-gene control used in Group L.
references.quote: We propose a normalization strategy, remove unwanted variation (RUV), that adjusts for nuisance technical effects by performing factor analysis on suitable sets of control genes (e.g., ERCC spike-ins) or samples (e.g., replicate libraries).
